sources.title: Tidal forces in Kiselev black hole, freely falling tetrad and geodesic deviation (2017)
Tidal forces in dirty black hole spacetimes, geodesic deviation (2022)
CERN-hosted review on black-hole test-particle tidal relative acceleration, arXiv 2202.04658

initial_conditions.metric: Schwarzschild non-rotating spherical spacetime; single E=1 radial reference geodesic
initial_conditions.separations: Jacobi fields between independently freely falling neighboring probes, NOT a solid rigid physical material body
initial_conditions.tetrad: Parallel transported orthonormal basis along radial freely falling reference observer
initial_conditions.initial_clock: Observer released from rest at infinity, already inward-moving when reaches 100 rs

mathematical_method.tidal_trace: radial + two tangential coefficients = zero (vacuum instant)
mathematical_method.u_time: T(r) = 2 rs/(3c)*(r/rs)^(3/2), formal remaining time to r=0
mathematical_method.volume_factor: Jacobi radial multiplier times transverse multiplier squared, no material properties
mathematical_method.extra_stop: r >= Bound11 declared K*lp^4=1; no underlying metric solution claimed beyond
mathematical_method.chosen_threshold_status: 1% is a deterministic modeling choice, not a material rupture threshold or physical law
mathematical_method.limit_order: For each finite initial probe size, the smallness test fails before the extreme curvature stop

interpretation_limits: Geodesic deviation is infinitesimal. Its analytic extension beyond a 1% local smallness test is diagnostic only, not a trustworthy extended-object separation.
At the horizon no physical discontinuity in the tidal eigenvalues occurs. A Schwarzschild-coordinate singularity is not a local tidal singularity.
The model tracks freely falling independent test particles, not a body with material elasticity or a tensile breaking threshold.
Some modeled values inside a black hole horizon are Schwarzschild classical extrapolations; quantum effects, accretion, spin, and backreaction remain unresolved.
Relative acceleration coefficients are measured in the locally falling frame; the reference geodesic has zero proper acceleration.
The radial/ transverse shape factors are relative lengths in a linearized local frame, not coordinates on a global toroidal surface.
24! index, 729 logarithmic addresses and shared train direction are independent computational selectors, not physical clock ticks or gravitational force relays.
Actual Sgr A* spin is not modeled, so no Kerr tetrad or frame dragging conclusion is supported.
Resizing the initial probe separation changes the validity boundary, illustrating a modeling dependence, not a universal singular surface.
next_bound: Bound 13: quantify local finite-body stress only after selecting actual material parameters and object length; separately compare rotating Kerr tidal eigenvalues against Schwarzschild in a matched local tetrad. Preserve the linearized validity and Planck curvature gates.
